notes: This is one handwritten English letter sheet on printed Harvard University stationery, dated Aug 4, 1969, addressed Dear Grothendieck. Four body paragraphs are present. There is no signature, closing, manuscript title or author page number on this sheet; 53 at the lower left is an archive number and is recorded only as a comment. The quoted work is Exposé V. Systèmes projectifs J-adiques, par J.P. Jouanolou. A boxed two-line pencil instruction at the upper right reads Faire copie / pour Jouanolou, with the surname still marked uncertain, and a pencil vertical line marks part of the first paragraph. The writer says I suppose of the attribution of the notes to one of the recipient's seminars and asks which seminar they belong to and whether there is a more recent edition. He explicitly says he does not understand the proof of the Theorem of Shih, calls the equivalence of (i) and (ii) not clear, and extends doubt to A.3.2 and Prop. 5.3.1. He says the difficulties would disappear in pro-A rather than the finer category P_AR. He asks about biregularity for a finite filtration and says I think the last hypothesis should use n and n+1 instead of n and n-1. These claims and author doubts are transcribed, not verified. H is description-only and is unavailable as a transcription: all h_reading values are null and every diff_h is false. Its description attributes the letter to R. Hartshorne and calls it the first of two sheets; neither the authorship nor the second sheet was independently checked here, so handwriting identities are not inferred in the inventory. The note and margin line are reproduced in TikZ; their rendering changes from C have the same semantic content and are not counted as substantive differences. The only substantive changes from C are the definite period after p. 40, the definite visible dot above the first minus, and the added throughtout alternative at the retraced word. All remaining C doubts are retained explicitly.
